title: Separator
description: Dividing sections, menu groups, and toolbars.
docs:
## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/separator ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | separator | `@components/cadence/separator/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: separator](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Separator needs only the two files and packages listed above; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required. Keep `separator/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` at the listed relative paths so the shared `cn` import resolves. All examples on this page use Separator alone and need no additional dependencies. A vertical separator needs a parent with a defined height, as shown in the Vertical example. ## Usage ```tsx import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator"; export function Account() { return (

Here its full height comes from the explicitly sized row; it keeps the vertical orientation in the accessibility tree. ```tsx import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator"; export function DraftBoundary() { return (

Cadence UI Made for your next project.
); } ``` ## When to use - Between groups inside a menu, a card footer, or a settings list. - Between a toolbar and its content, horizontally or vertically. - Inside a stack of sections that would otherwise merge visually. ## When not to use - To create space. Use padding or `gap`; a rule is a boundary, not a spacer. - Between every list item. Repetition turns a boundary into noise — grouped spacing does the same job with less ink. - As a decorative flourish in a hero. That is a background, not a separator. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Direction of the rule. | | `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders `role="none"` and `aria-hidden`; additive to upstream. | | `render` | Base UI render prop | – | Composition, as on every Base UI primitive. | | `className` | string or state callback | – | Merged last. | `data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation` are always set, so a consumer can size the rule from CSS: `data-[orientation=vertical]:h-8`. Base UI state callbacks for `className` are evaluated before merging caller classes last. `style` accepts an object or a state callback and is forwarded to the primitive. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A boundary that animates draws the eye to the wrong thing; if the layout changes, the surrounding `accordion` or `collapsible` owns that animation. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is the correct semantic for a group boundary. - `decorative` removes it from the accessibility tree for rules that carry no meaning (a divider inside a visual layout). - Focusable separators are not supported on purpose: a rule is not a control. ## Responsiveness and performance Horizontal separators fill available width; vertical separators need a parent with a defined height. Orientation is caller-owned, with no automatic breakpoint. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Prefer `gap` and `space-y` first; add a separator only when two groups need a visible boundary. - Never place a separator between two items of the same list. Group the list instead.
